changes.text: I got a smaller and much less romantic test later. Bee gave me some shoes to try that didn’t fit. I wore them for a day, and somehow my knee ended up messed up for about a month. She did nurse me, but a bit reluctantly. She also kept suggesting it was partly in my head, or not really that bad. I get it, neither of us could believe one day in the wrong shoes could do that, but it still felt like she was brushing me off because she wanted my knee to be fine.

findings.now: Grab it only if it really is the simplest explanation of what happened, and even the curiosity about that can be therapeutic for you.
findings.published: Don’t grab that story just because it makes everything easier to explain, and don’t reject it if it really is the most parsimonious explanation.
findings.why: the published two-sided warning (don't grab it for convenience, don't reject it when it is the simplest) becomes a one-sided condition, and "the curiosity about that" has a loose referent.
